slides.title: Cloud and Infrastructure Models
points: Architecture choices change who manages security, where systems run, how quickly they scale, and which third parties enter the trust boundary.

slides.title: Cloud
slides.teach: Computing resources delivered through a provider rather than hosted entirely on local infrastructure.

course.learn: Computing resources delivered through a provider rather than hosted entirely on local infrastructure.

breakdown.explanation: Computing resources delivered through a provider rather than hosted entirely on local infrastructure.
IaaS, PaaS, or SaaS, Provider-hosted workloads

course.why: This concept changes the security tradeoffs of the architecture.
course.check_q: What is the key exam clue for Cloud?

slides.title: Responsibility Matrix
slides.teach: Defines which security responsibilities belong to the cloud provider and which remain with the customer.

course.learn: Defines which security responsibilities belong to the cloud provider and which remain with the customer.

breakdown.explanation: Defines which security responsibilities belong to the cloud provider and which remain with the customer.
Provider secures physical infrastructure, Customer secures identities and data

course.why: This concept changes the security tradeoffs of the architecture.
course.check_q: What is the key exam clue for Responsibility Matrix?

slides.title: Hybrid Considerations
slides.teach: Security considerations created when an organization uses both on-premises and cloud resources.

course.learn: Security considerations created when an organization uses both on-premises and cloud resources.

breakdown.explanation: Security considerations created when an organization uses both on-premises and cloud resources.
Identity synchronization, Consistent logging across environments

course.why: This concept changes the security tradeoffs of the architecture.
course.check_q: What is the key exam clue for Hybrid Considerations?

slides.title: Third-party Vendors
slides.teach: External organizations whose products or services become part of the enterprise architecture and risk profile.

slides.title: Infrastructure as Code (IaC)
slides.teach: Uses machine-readable configuration files to provision and manage infrastructure consistently.

course.learn: Uses machine-readable configuration files to provision and manage infrastructure consistently.

breakdown.explanation: Uses machine-readable configuration files to provision and manage infrastructure consistently.

course.why: This concept changes the security tradeoffs of the architecture.
course.check_q: What is the key exam clue for Infrastructure as Code (IaC)?

slides.title: Serverless
slides.teach: A cloud model where the provider manages the underlying servers and the customer focuses primarily on code and configuration.

course.learn: A cloud model where the provider manages the underlying servers and the customer focuses primarily on code and configuration.

breakdown.explanation: A cloud model where the provider manages the underlying servers and the customer focuses primarily on code and configuration.

course.check_q: What is the key exam clue for Serverless?

slides.title: Microservices
slides.teach: An application design that breaks functionality into smaller independent services.

breakdown.explanation: An application design that breaks functionality into smaller independent services.

slides.title: On-premises
slides.teach: Infrastructure owned or operated directly within the organization's environment.

blocks.title: Cloud and Infrastructure Models exam shortcuts
items: Provider vs. customer duties → RESPONSIBILITY MATRIX
Use it to determine who secures each layer.
Example: Provider secures physical servers; customer secures identities.
Secure both environments and the connection between them.
Example: Shared identity spans SaaS and local systems.
Example: Terraform builds networks and VMs.
The provider manages the underlying servers.
Example: Code runs only when triggered.
Small services communicating over APIs → MICROSERVICES
Example: Auth and payment run separately.
blocks.example: Choose the architecture based on the security tradeoff emphasized in the scenario.

questions.q: A company uses cloud applications and an internal data center and must keep identity and logging consistent across both. Which concept is most relevant?
questions.explanation: Hybrid environments combine cloud and on-premises resources.

questions.q: A security team needs to know whether the cloud provider or customer must secure a specific layer. What should they consult?
questions.explanation: The responsibility matrix clarifies provider versus customer duties.

questions.q: A team deploys networks and virtual machines from version-controlled Terraform files. Which model is this?
Developers deploy functions while the provider manages the servers. Which architecture is this?
questions.explanation: Serverless removes direct server management from the customer.

questions.q: An application is split into separate authentication, payment, and inventory services. Which model is this?
questions.explanation: Microservices divide applications into smaller independent services.
